# `Q-5-23` — Alias Would Overwrite a Rendered Page

> An `aliases:` entry resolves to a path where the project renders
> a page. Writing the redirect stub there would replace that page,
> so the render stops instead.

## What this means

Each entry in a page's `aliases:` list becomes a small redirect
file in the output directory, so an old URL keeps working after
the page moves. This error fires when that redirect file would be
written on top of a real page.

Only one file can exist at a path. If the redirect were written,
the page would be gone from the built site and every visitor to it
would be bounced elsewhere.

## Why this happens

Usually the alias was never updated after a reorganization:

```yaml
---
title: Deployment
aliases:
  - /index.html   # but index.qmd renders here
---
```

It also happens when two pages swap places and each keeps the
other's old URL as an alias.

## How to fix it

Point the alias at a path no page renders to, or delete it if the
page it named no longer exists. If you genuinely want visitors to
land on the other page, edit that page instead of redirecting to
it — a redirect and a page cannot share a URL.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 detects the same situation, prints a warning, and skips
the redirect. Quarto 2 treats it as an error.

The reason is what the warning leaves behind: a site that builds
"successfully" while silently missing a redirect the author
believes exists. Old links keep 404ing, and nothing in the output
says why. A failed render that names the problem is recoverable in
a minute; a missing redirect can go unnoticed for months.
